mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY change < -2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% per month for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (not directly observed but inferred from yield curve inversion proxies) signals a flattening yield curve, which historically precedes equity market weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while long-term yields fall (implied from market data)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of yield curve flattening inferred from FEDFUNDS movements and external yield data.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 50,000 jobs in a month signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by > 50,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by more than 50,000 in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when INDPRO rises by at least 0.4% per month for six consecutive months.
